## Goal
`letters.render` (`src/freemyid/engine/letters.py:40-53`) uses a `SandboxedEnvironment` with autoescape off (27-29), and `split_subject` (81-85) takes the first line as the email subject. `tests/test_outbox_letters.py` and `tests/test_state_law_letters.py` test wording and citations, not hostile profile values.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Test: for every template in `TEMPLATES` (22-23), rendered with `letter_vars` (127-) for a fake profile whose name, city, nicknames and listing URLs contain `{{ 7*7 }}`, `{% for x in range(9) %}x{% endfor %}` and `{{ ''.__class__ }}`, the literal text comes out unchanged and nothing is evaluated.
2. Test and fix: CR/LF or other control characters inside profile values (`Jane\r\nBcc: x@evil.example`) never produce an extra header line. The subject returned by `split_subject` has no CR, LF or other control character, and no body line starting `Bcc:`, `Cc:` or `To:` comes from profile data. Fix inside `letters.py` (for example normalise control characters in the variables `letter_vars`/`value_letter_vars` build, and make `split_subject` collapse any stray line breaks); templates in `src/freemyid/templates/` are in-house and must not change.
3. Every email template's first line starts with `Subject:` (docstring line 7), and each renders with the defaults plus its required variables without a StrictUndefined error.
4. Unknown and path-like template names (`../x`, `ccpa.txt.j2/..`, `_identity`) raise `ValueError` (`_resolve` 32-37).
5. Existing letter tests still pass unchanged.

This is Codex code-lane work (owner, 2026-11-09): fix and improve the listed module(s) directly, with tests; don't xfail a bug you can fix here. No contract changes: public function signatures, `src/freemyid/models.py`, `interfaces.py`, schema files, `--json` shapes and documented CLI output stay as they are (additive helpers inside the listed files are fine). If the work turns out to need a contract change, stop and say so in VENDOR_STATUS.md "Questions for the owner". Fake data only, offline (fake fetchers, no network), Windows-safe paths in tests (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`, no `/tmp`). Typed, ruff-clean, small diff. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them.
